segments.english: All the more so, a fortiori, regarding our God, blessed be He, and blessed be His name, that the Torah insisted that one should not attach to Him or associate with Him anything of all created things, whether corporeal or spiritual, as it is said: "He who sacrifices to the gods shall be destroyed, save to the LORD alone." And Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna, peace be upon him, said: whoever associates the name of Heaven with something else is uprooted from the world. and we should not say that He is one as the others are one, since the Torah has made clear plainly in many places that He is one, unique, apart from all the other ones. Thus, you who mention the LORD should not think it right to refrain from making known His oneness, may He be blessed, to your children and your disciples, as you are commanded.

tokens.note: The two Talmudic forms of the a fortiori argument: כל שכן ('all the more so') and וקל וחומר ('light and heavy').
The verb is paired with לשתף below; the English renders it as attaching one thing to another.
כלא חד is an Aramaic-style idiom, literally 'as one'; rendered by its sense in the context.
The Tetragrammaton as written, ה׳: 'the LORD'.
להודיע: to make known. The clause אל דמי לכם מלהודיע is 'let it not seem right to you to refrain from making known'.

grammar: כל שכן and וקל וחומר are the two Talmudic forms of the a fortiori argument, and the English names the argument once, at the start.
The שלא clause depends on הקפידה: the Torah insisted that one not attach to God or associate with Him anything created.
Exod 22:19 is quoted with שנאמר, an explicit quotation, so it takes double quotation marks; the verse itself is in the apparatus.
ולא אמרינן כלא חד כיון ש… is the reasoning: since the Torah has made clear that He is one, we may not speak of Him as one of the ones.
הנה כן המזכירים את ה׳ is an address in the second person to the reader; אל דמי לכם is 'it should not seem to you'.
segments.note: Rendered by sense: כלא חד is the one clause whose sense is taken from its context; the literal is 'as one'.
apparatus: Exod 22:19, quoted with שנאמר: זובח לאלהים יחרם בלתי לה׳ לבדו. The author writes לה׳ where the verse has ליהוה; the English gives 'the LORD'.

segments.english: This book, The Wars of the LORD, makes known the way of the truths of His unity, may He be blessed, according to the Torah and its interpreters, our Rabbis of blessed memory, in the Mishnah, in the Bavli and the Yerushalmi, and the Midrashim of our Rabbis of blessed memory, and in accordance with the view of the Geonim, Rabbi Saadia Gaon, and our Rabbi Bahya in Chovot ha-Levavot, and Rabbi Yehuda Halevi in his poems, and in the Kuzari, the Rambam, the SeMaG and the author of the Ikkarim, of blessed memory, and as is accepted by every Jew. In it is a severe warning not to worship any created thing, in accordance with the tradition of all our prophets and all our sages, the Tannaim, the Amoraim, the Geonim and the early decisors, who received it from the mouth of Moses, Aaron and the elders, not to deviate from them and not to add to them.

tokens.note: The title: The Wars of the LORD (Num 21:14), as the title page gives it.
Bavli: the Babylonian Talmud.
Yerushalmi: the Jerusalem Talmud.
Chovot ha-Levavot, 'Duties of the Hearts', by Bahya.
Yehuda Halevi, poet and author of the Kuzari.
The Kuzari, Halevi's dialogue set at the court of the Khazar king.
SeMaG: an abbreviation for the medieval code Sefer Mitzvot Gadol.
Ikkarim: 'Principles', the book of the principles of faith.
The Hebrew is the word for Kabbalah. The author claims it here, for the chain of tradition from the prophets and sages, not for the Kabbalists.
From the mouth of: the chain Moses, Aaron and the elders.

grammar: The sentence has the subject ספר with the participle המודיע and the object דרך אמתות יחודו; the rest is a list of sources.
The list is joined by ו and by ב (in): 'in the Mishnah', 'in the Bavli', 'in the Kuzari'.
ובו אזהרה חמורה שלא לעבוד: 'and in it a severe warning not to worship'; the שלא clause gives the content of the warning.
כפי קבלת … מפי משה ואהרן וזקנים לא לזוז מהם ולא להוסיף עליהם: the chain of tradition ends in two infinitives, 'not to deviate' and 'not to add'.
segments.note: Title per the decisions (Q1). The Geonim and the Kuzari are given as context.
apparatus: Num 21:14, the title: ספר מלחמת ה׳ (The Wars of the LORD), as the title page gives it.
context: The Geonim (singular Gaon) were the heads of the Babylonian academies in the centuries after the Talmud.
The Kuzari is set at the court of the king of the Khazars.

segments.english: Know, esteemed reader, that you will not grasp the intention of this book, unless you read and study all of it, for its author made nights as days, and labored and scrutinized many books, and drew from seas and rivers proofs strong as a cast mirror, and the matters did not come from his own opinion. Therefore I ask you, esteemed reader, that you not come with the fist of Esau, in mockery, but with the voice of Jacob, and to consider the matters, and whoever is lacking in strength, let him be silent from speech and be still, and may El Shaddai give you mercy, and the merit of the author will protect us, and upon all His people Israel.

ע״כ is read as ועל כל, 'and upon all', here. Elsewhere it closes a quotation or means 'thus far'.

grammar: ודע לך: an imperative with 'to you', 'know'; the author addresses the reader in the second person throughout.
לא תשיג כונת הספר הזה אלא אחרי שתקרא: 'you will not grasp… unless after you read…'.
כי מחברו עשה לילות כימים: the second כי is causal, 'for its author made nights as days'.
ולכן אבקשך שלא תבוא באגרונו של עשו בהתולים אלא בקולו של יעקב: the request contrasts the fist of Esau with the voice of Jacob.
segments.note: The allusion to Gen 27:22 is kept without quotation marks; the author's 'fist' is kept where the verse has 'hands'.
apparatus: Gen 27:22, an allusion without quotation marks: 'the voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau'. The author writes אגרון (fist) where the verse has ידים (hands).
